title: finding(types): objectui#7759 group F residue — `DashboardComponentSchema.dateRange` mirror is wider than its declaration (spec exports DATE_RANGE_DEFAULT_RANGES)
body:
This card is the residue of objectstack-ai/objectui#7759 **group F**. The objectui#10296 dev (PR objectui#10307) correctly STOPPED on this row, because it sat in PR objectui#10273's Dashboard-twin region. objectui#10273 landed on `main` as `1bbaa16`, so the row is now free to settle.

It was filed by the `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat, session `session_01877XiBYSaRCk2CU7cMSg3S`. Priority and domain are inherited from the parent (`priority:p2`, `domain:spec`).

## The row, on `main` `f3f4e4c`

- `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`: `WiderThanDeclared['complex.zod.ts#DashboardComponentSchema']` includes `'dateRange'`, and `WIDER_ARMS` has `complex.zod.ts#DashboardComponentSchema::dateRange: ['CONCRETE']`.
- The mirror is `complex.zod.ts`, about `:1196`: `dateRange: z.object({ … })`. `dateRange` is on `DASHBOARD_SPEC_EXCLUDED`, so objectui's own element schema is used.
- Measured in passing by the #10296 dev: `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 exports `DATE_RANGE_DEFAULT_RANGES` / `DateRangeDefaultRange` from `@objectstack/spec/ui`, so **rule 1 likely governs**. The mirror's `defaultRange` vocabulary should take the spec's, and the declaration should follow.

## Rules (#7759 ruling 5617465269 + ordering note 5617614225)

- rule 1: spec-declared means both faces align to the spec;
- rule 2: an objectui-own key follows its read site (`DashboardRenderer`);
- ordering: if the protocol is judged wrong, a spec card comes first and this card stops;
- F1: a structural mirror points at the spec's **authoring** schema, never a read model.

## Done when

The row leaves `WiderThanDeclared` / `WIDER_ARMS`, or is recorded as an expected divergence with its reason. A pin reddens on revert. One `@object-ui/types` changeset is added (`minor`, Clause-② yes).
